newsitem.title: USA: Gore challenges Dole on budget.
newsitem.headline: Gore challenges Dole on budget.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore Sunday challenged Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole to submit his proposed budget plan to the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) for a bipartisan analysis before the election.

Republican vice presidential candidate Jack Kemp, appearing on ABC's "This Week With David Brinkley," agreed to do it and said the Dole-Kemp campaign would submit their budget plan for scrutiny by the office.

Charging that the Dole budget plan would "blow a big hole in the deficit" and lead to cuts in Social Security and Medicare, Gore said, "I challenge Bob Dole and (House Speaker) Newt Gingrich to submit his budget plan to the Congressional Budget Office and ask for a response before the election."

Gore accused the two Republicans of failing to live up to a promise made by Gingrich that the budget plan featuring a 15 percent tax cut would be given to the budget office for a bipartisan analysis. The Congressional Budget Office provides analysis to both major political parties in Congress.

"We are going to balance the budget," Gore said on NBC's "Meet the Press" program, arguing that the Republican plan would wreak havoc with the budget deficit and force deeper cutbacks in essential services.

In New Jersey, where Dole was campaigning, spokesman Nelson Warfield said he hadn't yet seen Gore's remarks but "I think the CBO has said they are not in the business of doing that," analyzing a candidate's budget proposals.
On ABC, when asked about asking the CBO to analyze the Republican budget plan, Kemp replied: "I would be glad to ... yes, we'll do it."
On NBC, Gore also denied allegations the Clinton campaign had accepted illegal campaign contributions.
"We have strictly abided by all campaign laws," Gore said, although he conceded Clinton campaign officials had to turn back some sizeable contributions when they appeared to be questionable.
He said "there is absolutely no truth to that whatsoever" when asked about a report he had played a personal role in dealing with one of these questionable contributors.
Gingrich, campaigning in Georgia Saturday, cited an article in the Washington Post about a $425,000 Democratic campaign contribution from an Indonesian couple as suggesting a major political scandal.

"The president has been soliciting money from foreign nationals? The greatest power in the world being rented to foreigners? This is a scandal that has historic implications. It makes Watergate look trivial," Gingrich said.
